summary:
A year after National Guard troops were deployed to Washington, D.C., advocacy groups are highlighting the deployment as evidence for why statehood matters, while separately, a proposed sleeping ban at the MLK Library and threats to D.C.'s fiscal independence have drawn warnings from local advocates. The stories reflect ongoing concerns about federal control over D.C. governance and policy.

Without statehood, D.C. does not control its own National Guard and cannot refuse the deployment of other states' troops within its borders.
